doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Church music at home and the family's musical connection
summary: Only church music was heard at home; the siblings took lessons but Barry alone kept going, feeling the connection from age four.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So the music in the house when you were – you know, your first ten years. The music that you heard, what was some of the music that you heard?
Church music. Nothing but church music.
I think one time she did show me a little of the licks she used to do. [laughs]
They weren’t the church licks. [laughs] It wasn’t quite a church lick. But it was something, you know, so she knew a little something else, too.
Okay, alright. So then your siblings, how do they relate to the music? How was that relationship?

Um, all of us took up music some kind of way, you know. My sister and I – my youngest sister and I, we went to lessons. My brother wouldn’t too much. My other sister, she was into music. The oldest sister wasn’t. But um, about three of us, we took up music, you know. And um, I’m the one that ended up with music, you know. The only one. Um, they sort of dropped by thw wayside, you know. But um, I have continued the family tradition of music, you know. I’m just a continuation of Bessie, you know.
So you felt it early, the connection?
Oh yeah. I felt an early connection, see. My connection started at the age of four.
